newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian dlr ends trying to break higher.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian dlr ends trying to break higher.

text.p: The Australian dollar ended the week trying to make a sustained break above US$0.7940 as a step towards breaking out of its five week long US$0.7985/95 range.

The Australian dollar opened local trading above US$0.7930 on Friday, and held there through the morning, undisturbed by relatively flat September imports data, before making a later break above US$0.7940, traders said.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7943/48 from an early US$0.7933/38 and a Thursday close of US$0.7915/20. The unit traded a US$0.7932/47 range on the day.
Traders said the market had been quiet for most of the day, with volume slowing ahead of the weekend until the late strength as the European market opened.
Sellers had been capping the unit under US$0.7940, but the persistence of the buyers, and support under US$0.7930 saw the unit edge higher.
To break above US$0.7960, buying would need to remain fairly steady, as sellers were expected around US$0.7950.
On the crosses, the dollar closed firmer at 89.12/22 yen and 1.2241/51 marks from an opening 89.00/10 and 1.2235/47 and levels on late Tuesday of 88.60/70 and 1.2173/87.
The dollar closed at 58.8 in trade-weighted terms, its highest close since September 12, from an opening 58.7 and a previous close of 58.6.

Traders said while the dollar had benefitted overnight when the U.S. dollar was bought against the mark as a safe haven currency on news of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's sacking of his security chief Alexander Lebed, there was no specfic buying of the local unit against the mark today.
Merchandise imports rose 0.5 percent in September, against median expectations of a 1.0 percent rise. The data did suggest the economy remained soft, economists said.
"Today's numbers confirm easing import growth reflecting the slowing in domestic demand over 1996," Westpac senior economist John Peters said.

"Whilst the partial indicators are sending some mixed signals, the message from imports is unambiguously weak and supports our view that underlying economic activity is weak and running below potential," he said
As the data pointed to another current account deficit of around A$1.2 to A$1.4 billion, reaction was muted with attention focused on next week's third quarter inflation and wages data.
The key underlying inflation rate is expected to have risen 0.6 percent in the September quarter, seeing the annual rate moderate to 2.5 percent form 3.1 percent in June.
The Reserve Bank aims to keep the underlying rate to an average of between two and three percent over a run of years, and the improving inflation outlook was a factor behind the July 31 rate cut.

Another rate cut from the current 7.0 percent level had been widely expected in November if Thursday's wages data also showed signs of moderation, but those expectations were dented by the release of the RBA's bulletin on Wednesday.

Economists expect wages to have risen by 1.0 in the third quarter, with the annual rate falling to 3.7 percent from 3.9 percent. Such a result would still leave the door open for a November rate cut, some economists said.
Economists surveyed by Reuters said there was a 47.5 percent chance of the RBA cutting rates before the end of November, with 16 of the 32 surveyed putting the odds at 50 percent or more.
